findings.headline: Early‑race stress high but pace held; no stop needed
findings.detail: Stress spiked to 84.2 on lap 3 while the driver was on a 3‑lap‑old Medium tyre, in dry conditions and battling traffic (P13, 0.4s to car ahead). Pace delta was -0.03s, showing no loss despite the high stress. The strategy call correctly held the stop, confirming that early‑race stress did not merit a tyre change.

findings.headline: Wet‑track onset caused huge Medium tyre slowdown; consider earlier switch
findings.detail: From laps 19‑27 the Medium tyres suffered a massive pace delta jump (+8.832 s on lap 19) as the track went wet, yet stress readings are missing, suggesting the driver was not aware of the degradation. The modelled degradation (+0.219 s/lap) combined with the wet surface caused a 9‑second slowdown, indicating the need for an earlier tyre swap when rain first appeared.

findings.headline: Intermediate tyres performed well as track dried; blue‑flag traffic may hide degradation
findings.detail: During the Intermediate stint (laps 28‑38) the pace delta improved steadily to -1.856 s by lap 30, despite the tyres being only 3 laps old, indicating the modelled degradation (+0.114 s/lap) was offset by drying track. However, the driver received blue flags on laps 21‑27 and again on 34‑36, suggesting he was consistently overtaking slower cars, which may have masked the true tyre performance.

findings.headline: Soft tyres delivered consistent pace; driver stress low – strategy validated
findings.detail: The Soft tyre stint (laps 39‑52) shows a flat pace delta around 0.0 s with a slight dip to -0.190 s on lap 42, while the modelled degradation is only +0.107 s/lap. This suggests the Softs were operating near optimal grip despite the track drying, but the driver’s stress dropped to 27.3 post‑race, indicating low mental load. No performance loss observed, so the current Soft strategy is sound.

findings.headline: Blue‑flag traffic may hide stress spikes; consider adding stress monitoring
findings.detail: Blue‑flag periods on laps 21‑27 and 34‑36 coincided with modest pace improvements (+0.358 on lap 17 then -0.358 on lap 18) but no stress data, making it unclear if the driver was conserving effort. Given only a handful of calls, confidence is limited, but monitoring stress during blue‑flag traffic could prevent hidden fatigue.

findings.headline: Driver handled cooling track well; need more stress data to confirm
findings.detail: The track temperature fell from 33.0 C at start to 20.7 C by lap 30, yet pace delta improved dramatically during the Intermediate stint, implying the driver adapted well to cooling conditions. However, with only one stress reading in dry conditions, we cannot confirm mental adaptation; further stress sampling would improve confidence.
